design.prompt: Anime cel-shaded character art in the style of Studio Trigger's Cyberpunk Edgerunners: flat muted colors, bold clean black outlines, hard-edged two-tone shading, at most one small lit accent. Full body, strict side view facing right, the whole figure from the top of the head to the soles inside the frame, tall in the frame: the figure fills nine tenths of the picture height. The character stands upright and still, like a model sheet: weight evenly on both feet, hips and shoulders level, the spine vertical, the chest not pushed out and the lower back not arched, the head level. The near arm hangs straight down beside the thigh with an open empty hand; it is not swept back. The far arm is hidden behind the torso. The feet are a small step apart with the far foot half a step ahead, so the far shin and the far shoe show in front of the near leg. Egret, a veteran harbour mercenary, a woman of forty-six, clearly a woman: a woman's face, jaw and neck, a woman's lean athletic build under the work clothes; about seven heads tall, rangy with long legs. Cropped steel-grey hair shaved at the side with a longer swept top, weathered tan skin, laugh lines, a thin old scar across the cheekbone, a crooked half-grin. She wears a faded slate-grey oilskin rain jacket that ends at the belt, zipped half way with the collar turned up, the sleeves down to the wrists, one elbow patched; a dark work shirt; worn canvas cargo trousers with a knee patch, tucked into scuffed black rubber dock boots; fingerless work gloves; a folded black umbrella slung across her back on a strap; one short teal reflective strip on the jacket sleeve. Empty hands. Uneven rough hand-inked linework with varied line weight, gritty grime and fabric wrinkles where the cloth bends, slightly asymmetrical, lived-in and worn, matte not glossy, not airbrushed, no idealized perfect face. Few large plain shapes, no decorative details beyond the ones described. Even overcast light, no glow, no bloom, no text.
